findings.title: Event listener calls V2 setPermissionsEnabled which always throws UnsupportedOperationException
findings.body: registerListener gates on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) being enabled, but when V2 is also enabled (the normal way V2 is used), management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients().setPermissionsEnabled(), roles().setPermissionsEnabled() (inherited V1 paths) / groups().setPermissionsEnabled() paths route to the V2 implementations that throw UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported in V2'). Concretely, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (line 193) always throws. So whenever both features are enabled together, a ClientRemovedEvent / RoleRemovedEvent / GroupRemovedEvent fired during normal admin operations will throw inside the provider event listener and break client/role/group deletion. The guard must also exclude the V2 case (or the V2 implementations must be no-ops) for these cleanup events.

findings.title: NPE when per-client resource is absent and the 'Clients' type resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String) (lines 214-222), when resourceStore.findByName for the client-specific resource returns null, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately dereferences it via authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). However getResourceTypeResource can return null (e.g., when supportsAuthorizationSchema is false because admin permissions are disabled in the realm or the resource server is not the admin-permissions client, or when the resource type lookup fails). Passing a null resource to findByResource causes an NPE instead of a clean 'no permission' result, so admin endpoints evaluating client permissions can fail with a 500 instead of 403.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission includes the 'all clients' resource name 'Clients' in the returned client-id set
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates resources found by type Clients and adds resource.getName() to the granted set. The resource-type resource created at schema init is named 'Clients' (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and is also of that type, so when a type-level permission grants the scope, the literal string 'Clients' is added to the set alongside real client IDs. Callers using this set to filter clients by ID will never match a client with id 'Clients', effectively breaking the 'manage all clients' case for permission-based list filtering. The type-level resource should be detected and handled as a wildcard rather than added as a client id.

findings.title: getResourceName returns null display name for client resources
findings.body: getResourceName was extended with the Clients resource type in the schema, but its implementation only handles USERS: for a Clients policy on a per-client resource it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null because per-client resources are created with only a name (the client's ID) in getOrCreateResource (resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()), line 104). Any admin UI/REST rendering of client scope-permission resources will show a null/empty name instead of the client's clientId, unlike the Users case which resolves and returns the username. A branch resolving the client by ID and returning client.getClientId() is missing.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports (getEvaluationContext, TOKEN_EXCHANGE, Scope, EvaluationContext, logger)
findings.body: The private method getEvaluationContext and the imports TOKEN_EXCHANGE, Scope, EvaluationContext, ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext, and the logger field are unused in this class. This is leftover from token-exchange support which is explicitly not implemented in V2 (canExchangeTo throws). Dead code around an unimplemented security-relevant feature invites confusion about whether token-exchange permission evaluation is actually performed; it should be removed.
